titre_page: How to make a platformer in Yop2D: full no-code tutorial | Yop2D Guide
description: Step-by-step tutorial to make a small no-code platformer with Yop2D: ground, a hero who jumps, pearls to collect, a patrolling enemy and a score.
carte: A hero, pearls to collect, a turtle to avoid and a score.
etapes: Place the background and the ground
A background, a ground with the "Ground / wall" behavior and a raised block.
An animated character with the "Platform character" behavior, a joystick and a jump button.
An enemy with the "Patrol (back and forth)" behavior and the tag ennemi.
Three pearls with the tag piece.
A score variable and a text that displays it.
Collect the three pearls to win.
blocs: In this tutorial you make a **small platformer** in about half an hour, without writing any code: a hero who runs and jumps, **three pearls** to collect, a **turtle** that walks back and forth on a block, and a **score**. If you get stuck, compare with the [finished project](https://zinzin66.github.io/Yop2d-web/tests/plateforme-tuto-test.zip) (import it into Yop2D: its nodes are tidied up with frames and sticky notes that explain everything).
Screenshot of the platformer: the hero, pearls, a turtle on a block and the score at the top left
The finished game: the score is at the top left.
an empty game in **landscape** (tap **New game** on the start screen);
the images of the **Prehistory** theme in the **Yop2D Library** (free, royalty-free): background, ground, hero, turtle and pearl;
a little time: every step is short.
The screenshots are in English. On your device the same buttons are written in the language of Yop2D, in the same place.
Step 1: the background, the ground and a block

Tap **Object** (top left), then **Image**. The **Yop2D Library** opens: choose the **Prehistory** theme, the **Backgrounds** folder, then the **jungle** background. It places itself behind everything.
Do **Object → Image** again and take a **grass ground** in **Ground and platforms**. Place it at the very bottom and stretch it across the screen. Name it **sol** in the inspector.
Tap **⚙ Behavior** (in the inspector) and choose **Ground / wall**: the hero will walk on it and not fall through.
Add a small **grass platform** and place it higher, on the right, about 150 pixels above the ground. Give it the **Ground / wall** behavior too. Name it **bloc**.
Object behavior window of the ground object with "Ground / wall" selected
The "Ground / wall" behavior: the object does not move, you walk on it.
The hero jumps about 200 pixels high: a block 150 pixels above the ground is easy to reach. If you place it higher, you will need another platform to climb.

**Object → Image → Library**, **Prehistory** theme, **Characters** folder. Choose the caveman with **With its animations**: the image and the animations (idle, walk…) are added at once. Put him on the ground and name him **player**.
**⚙ Behavior → Platform character**: he walks, jumps and falls.

Add a {{lang:obj_prefix_joystick}} at the bottom left and a round **button** at the bottom right for jumping. In the behavior window, choose this button as the **jump button**. The guide [Moving a character](guide:deplacer-personnage)" explains the joystick and jumping.
Object behavior window of the player object with "Platform character" selected
The "Platform character" behavior for the hero.
Yop2D editor with markers: Object button, object list, Behavior card, Play button
The editor: 1 the **Object** button to add things, 2 the **list of objects** in the scene, 3 the **Behavior** card of the selected object, 4 the **Play** button.
Tap **Play** (4) to try: the hero should walk, jump and stay on the ground. Tap ■ to go back to the editor.
**Object → Image → Library**, **Prehistory** theme, **Monsters** folder: take the **turtle** and place it **on the block**. Name it **tortue**.
**⚙ Behavior → Patrol (back and forth)**: it walks by itself one way then the other and turns around at the edge of the block. No node needed.
In the inspector, **For the nodes** section, write the tag **ennemi**. You will need it in step 6.
Object behavior window of the turtle with "Patrol" selected
The "Patrol (back and forth)" behavior: perfect for an enemy.
On the block, leave a little room on each side of the turtle: it turns around just before the edge.
**Object → Image → Library**, **Prehistory** theme, **Objects** folder: take the **gold pearl**. Place it within jumping reach, for example on the ground. Name it **piece1**.
In the inspector, **For the nodes** section, write the tag **piece** (no accent, all lowercase).

Tap **Copy** (at the top) twice: the copies appear near the original. Move them: one in the air above the ground, the last one **above the block**, high enough that the turtle cannot touch it. They keep the same tag **piece**.
Inspector of the pearl piece1 showing the tag piece
The tag **piece** on each pearl: one single rule will serve all three.
A **tag** is a family name. Here the three pearls share the same one, so you only build the nodes once.
In the left panel, **Variables** section, tap **+** and create a variable **score**: type **integer**, starting value **0**, **local** to the scene.

**Object → Text**: write **Pièces : 0**, put it at the top left and name it **texteScore**. To keep it readable, make it bigger (font size 60 to 70); if you put a small **dark panel** behind it, check that the text is **in front** (its **Z** must be higher than the panel's).
Left panel of the editor with the score variable and the plus button
The **score** variable (1) is created with the **+** button.

Now tell the game what happens when the hero touches something. Tap **Blueprint** (top right): the node screen opens. To place a node, open a category on the left and tap it; to connect two nodes, drag a wire from the output of the first to the input of the next.

**When the hero touches a pearl.** Place the {{NoeudEventCollisionTag}} event: **Object A** = **player**, **Tag** = **piece**. Connect, in order: {{detruire_objet}} (on **The involved object**, i.e. the pearl just touched), {{ajouter_variable}} (variable **score**, value **1**), then {{modifier_texte}} (object **texteScore**, text written with the value `="Pièces : " + score`, which shows the score).

**When the score reaches 3.** Add a {{condition}} node after it with `=score >= 3`. On its **True** output, connect: {{modifier_texte}} (texteScore, text **BRAVO**), {{attendre}} (6 seconds) then {{recommencer_scene}}.

**When the hero touches the turtle.** A second {{NoeudEventCollisionTag}} event: **Object A** = **player**, **Tag** = **ennemi**. After it: {{flash_ecran}}, {{toast}} (a small "Ouch!" message), {{attendre}} (1 second) then {{recommencer_scene}}.
**Stay inside the screen.** A {{NoeudEventChaqueImage}} event connected to {{garder_dans_ecran}} (object **player**) keeps the hero from leaving the level.
Settings window of the "If an object touches a tag" node: Object A player, Tag piece
The event's settings window: 1 the object that touches (**player**), 2 the tag touched (**piece**).
Blueprint screen of the game: three groups of nodes in colored frames with sticky notes
The finished Blueprint: one frame per idea (pearls, enemy, stay inside the screen).
In a node's window you do not have to type object names: tap them in the left list. Remember to **save** (💾) before going back to the editor.

Tap **Play**. Run, jump, collect the pearls: the text at the top left counts them. Climb onto the block to take the last pearl without touching the turtle. After three pearls, **BRAVO** appears, then the game restarts.
The game after three pearls: the text BRAVO at the top left
Add more pearls, turtles and blocks: the nodes you already built keep working thanks to the **tags**.
Add **sounds** (a "ding" for each pearl) with the {{jouer_son}} node, or a background **music**.
Give the hero **lives**: [Losing lives and game over](guide:vie-game-over).
Go to a **next level** when you win: [Going to the next level](guide:niveau-suivant).
